momo.session: morning session: 10 specs run (budget used today: 10 of 20), 3 robust runs, 0 nominations
notes: Setup note: the momo checkout had been recreated at 07:18 without `.venv`; rebuilt it with `python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt` (gitignored, checkout stayed clean). Main pulled to 6f70d54.

Lessons: (1) Slow, wide exits are what make nudges pass (trend-hold-regime); tight crosses (cmf, avwap dist) make sharp peaks. (2) Ranking by rel_strength concentrates in TSLA/CAR and large caps; the next refinement of trend-hold-regime should change the rank, e.g. rank by obv_trend or -atr_pct or default liquidity, or cap rs (entry rs < some ceiling) so one parabolic name can't dominate. (3) Sectors are the hardest gate: trend strategies trail sector equal-weight in staples, comm services, IT…

momo.session: afternoon session: 10 specs run (budget used today: 20 of 20), 1 robust run, 0 nominations
notes: Main at 210c15c (cup_handle_stage merged). Checkout stayed clean.

Lessons: (1) Non-rs ranks (-atr, obv) cut TSLA concentration and lift Sharpe/DD but systematically sacrifice CAGR below SPY — need a rank that preserves return, not just diversity (maybe default liquidity, or soft rs cap). (2) cup_handle / stage-5 fires too rarely on discovery broad (~10% exposure); next cup work needs denser staging (e.g. hold from stage>=3 with volume confirm) or looser pattern params as the primary knob, not just exit style. (3) sma-cross-wide is the first mid/trend cross id…

The 10:37 routine failed before any trial: the checkout's `.venv` was missing. Rebuilt it at the start of the afternoon session (`python3 -m venv .venv && pip install -r requirements.txt`; `.venv/` is gitignored, so git stays clean). If a run errors on `.venv/bin/python`, rebuild the same way.

snapback.session: afternoon session: 10 specs run (budget used today: 10 of 20), 0 robust runs, 0 nominations
notes: Main at 210c15c (adds cup_handle_stage). Refinements first, each aimed at what broke:
New ideas:

Lessons: the rising-SMA50 filter is not a portable edge. It hurt both the ROC dip and the MFI reclaim, and every trigger I paired it with today lagged SPY. vwap-reclaim-rising looks like a single-setting fit: making the reclaim smoother killed it, so stop refining it. The one useful finding is the quiet-pullback filter (ATR%(10) < ATR%(50)), which cut rs-pullback-roc's DD to 13% but starved exposure. Next session: build on rs-pullback-roc's original SMA200 form (still the best near-miss, 0.925)…
